subject.title: Feature: configurable bootstrap file injection order for prompt cache optimization

question: Should OpenClaw expose configurable bootstrap dynamic-file classification and file ordering in core config, or should this be solved through a context-engine/plugin API instead?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but adding bootstrap ordering/dynamic classification creates a public prompt/config contract in an area where repository policy sets a high bar for new config surfaces.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow core contract
options.body: Add documented core config for dynamic bootstrap files and order, with schema/types/docs and upgrade-safe tests around prompt-cache boundary placement.

options.title: Extend plugin/context-engine APIs
options.body: Keep core config unchanged and add or document an extension point that lets a plugin own volatility metadata and ordering without renaming files.

options.title: Defer to operator patterns
options.body: Leave the request open or close by maintainer decision after documenting current mitigations such as smaller `MEMORY.md`, `contextInjection`, and context engines.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a narrow core contract
recommendation.body: Add documented core config for dynamic bootstrap files and order, with schema/types/docs and upgrade-safe tests around prompt-cache boundary placement.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent authored the existing stable/dynamic heartbeat ordering and adjacent context-injection work, making him the strongest routing candidate for this product/API choice.
